# Native Muscle Excitation Replay

## Status and Scope

Provisional development evidence for F07/F08 (#11791/#11792), not a qualified
full-swing result. `tour_matching.muscle_replay` runs a fresh native OpenSim
model from every named continuous initial state. The early implementation
supports muscle forces and gravity only. Non-muscle actuators, other forces
(including contact forces pending their explicit policy), pre-existing
controllers, prescribed motion/coordinates, locks and unsupported constraints
are rejected through recursive component auditing, including components outside
legacy ForceSet/ControllerSet containers. Recursively owned muscle paths must
match the native muscle registry, preventing an undeclared undriven muscle. The early muscle-law domain policy
supports Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle and Thelen2003Muscle with active activation
and compliant tendon dynamics. Ignored activation/tendon modes fail before
native initialization; other laws require explicit domain qualification.
Initial and sampled trajectory activation/fiber state must respect each native
instance's minima without clipping, and fiber length must remain positive.
The zero-pennation Thelen fixture has a zero native minimum fiber length;
the Millard numerical floor must not be copied to it. Contact geometry counts
are metadata, not evidence of contact dynamics. Full anatomical/contact model
qualification and capture matching remain open.

## Equations and Input Boundary

For excitation samples $e_{i,k}$ at physical times $t_k$ in seconds, the native
time-only input player uses

$$e_i(t)=(1-\alpha)e_{i,k}+\alpha e_{i,k+1},\qquad
\alpha=(t-t_k)/(t_{k+1}-t_k).$$

Strictly increasing finite times and finite samples in $[0,1]$ ensure bounded
linear interpolation over the simulated interval. Excitation is dimensionless;
it is distinct from activation and the resulting force in newtons. Native
muscle activation and compliant-fiber dynamics evolve without state resets.
Configuration and speed retain the model's native coordinate conventions.
No muscle equilibration is applied after restoring supplied initial state.

## Numerical Method and Provenance

One native Manager cold-starts Runge-Kutta-Merson with an explicit accuracy
parameter (default $10^{-8}$) and advances continuously across output times.
The requested time grid is an output/input-knot grid, not the adaptive internal
step sequence. Both reference generation and reproduction must use the same
declared initialization policy. Named continuous states do not serialize
discrete/plugin state or integrator history; broader models remain unsupported
until their initialization is qualified.

The receipt binds model bytes, ordered native state and muscle names, full
continuous initial state, time grid, excitation samples, interpolation,
integrator accuracy, installed provider version and ordered concrete muscle
laws. Adapter `native-muscle-replay/1.3.1` binds the executed subtype policy and
`muscle_class_policy="exact-supported-concrete-law/1.0.0"`. Before native
`initSystem`, recursive admission requires exact concrete identity
`Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle` or `Thelen2003Muscle`. A successful base-class
`safeDownCast` establishes inheritance compatibility only; it cannot qualify an
unknown derived law's state or force semantics. Native casts remain in use for
the supported laws' model-owned state bounds. This guard does not broaden the
existing compliant-tendon, activation, force, constraint or initialization scope.
Native applied excitations
are checked at output times separately from native muscle forces. This local
receipt is a development adapter; the versioned Tools bundle remains the
durable interchange authority. The model file alone is not a complete hash of
arbitrary external resource dependencies. The OpenSim muscle-bundle adapter
therefore retains the unchanged T01 bundle for models without resources and
wraps resource-bearing bundles in the local versioned
`opensim-native-visual-resource-closure/1` envelope. That envelope admits only
source-declared `.vtp` `Mesh` objects owned by a body's `attached_geometry`;
each normalized relative path, component path, and asset SHA-256 is bound to
the source-model SHA-256. Admission rejects missing, changed, duplicate,
absolute, escaping, symlinked, or non-visual references. Replay copies the
source and exact assets into an owned temporary snapshot, rebuilds the closure,
and checks it again after native execution. The component-class exception is
limited to those exact source-owned visual meshes; visual geometry does not
authorize forces, contact, wrapping, or other mechanical inputs. This closure
establishes asset identity and native visual-component loading only. It does
not qualify wrapped/chart dynamics, contact, anatomical fidelity, or any
full-body result.

## Evidence and Limits

`tests/opensim/test_native_muscle_replay.py` creates a genuine one-DOF native
Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle and Thelen2003Muscle fixtures, including nonzero
activation and compliant fiber state. Tests check independent restored native
force, restoring muscle motion, native applied commands,
same-policy reproduction, tighter-accuracy/output-grid refinement and rejection
of invalid inputs, missing state and hidden drives. This is independent of
capture fitting and is not a physiological parameter validation.

Child #11867 adds a class-identity boundary test that substitutes an unknown
reported class on real native Component/Muscle proxies while retaining
successful native base casts. An initialization trap proves rejection precedes
`initSystem`. This is explicitly proxy boundary evidence, not a loaded or
compiled third-party C++ plugin test. Both unchanged concrete native laws retain
their positive replay tests. New subclasses need their own reviewed state,
force, serialization and initialization policy before admission.

Executed locally with OpenSim 4.6 (2026-06-22-85aaf64), Python 3.12.10:

```powershell
python3 -m pytest tests/opensim/test_native_muscle_replay.py --override-ini='addopts=' -q
```

Use an environment with the reported native provider; optional-provider skips
in other environments do not establish native acceptance. Full-body anatomy,
native contact force traces, grip and club dynamics, reserve audits, uncertainty,
full-horizon mocap accuracy and clean-host reproduction remain required gates.
See the binding [architecture review](../../../docs/development/feedback_controls/ASTRA_REVIEW.md).

## Native Law and Contact Integration

Main integration combines the listed native contact policy with both compliant
Millard and Thelen laws. Combined adapter version 1.3.1 retains ordered muscle laws,
model-owned state minima and every contact/force policy field. The combined
actual OpenSim4.6 suite passes106 cases; two extra-geometry tests are inapplicable
to SmoothSphereHalfSpace and are skipped explicitly. These synthetic probes do
not qualify full-body anatomy, capture matching or production contact.

## Bounded Synthetic Moco Solve and Independent Replay

The development-only Moco ladder in
`tests/opensim/native_moco_ladder_worker.py` uses a source-hashed synthetic
OpenSim model, not a golf capture. Its ten named initial states include the
base coordinate $q=0.3$ rad, dependent coordinate $2q=0.6$ rad, fixed anchor
$0.2$ rad, zero coordinate speeds, activation $0.05$ for each of two Millard
muscles, and their native fiber lengths $0.09541832200700395$ m and
$0.08545580283920036$ m. Muscle command bounds are read from the loaded source
(`min_control=0.01`, `max_control=1.0`) and bound into the request. A fixed
0.05 excitation forward integration creates a feasible trajectory guess; it
does not prescribe the subsequent optimized solution.
The exact source-model SHA-256 is
`6a098517bdba09b19b3eb99e4da7e795f27d10be8f42c0fca04fee20ce67e143`; the
native runs used OpenSim 4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64 with Python 3.12.10. The
retained runtime fingerprint covers the Python extensions and Moco DLL only;
it is not a closed hash of all transitive runtime libraries.

For horizon $T=0.01$ s, the optimization holds the cold initial state and
requires the base coordinate to reach
$q_f=0.30000558574001657$ rad, with coordinate bounds $[0.2,0.4]$ rad. It
minimizes the native Moco `effort` control goal. The request fixes
Hermite-Simpson transcription, midpoint control interpolation enabled,
parallelism 0, maximum 300 iterations, convergence tolerance $10^{-6}$ and
constraint tolerance $10^{-7}$. Mesh refinement from 10 to 20 intervals
changes the transcription mesh (21 versus 41 exported nodes); it retains the
same horizon, target, source, state, controls policy and tolerances. The
resulting time-only controls are reloaded from storage and applied to a fresh
native model using piecewise-linear interpolation.

Before interpreting a solve, source, provider, state, control and request
identities are bound; solver settings must match their native readback. The
serialized optimized time/state/control arrays must match the in-memory arrays
within eight representable float64 values per element, with exact endpoint
clock and strict clock/control shape checks. The observed solution export was
within three ULP. Independent replay checks all ten named states at saved
times, requires the initial state to match exactly, and requires both optimized
and replayed endpoints to reach the target in the positive direction. Maximum
optimized-to-replayed absolute errors must remain below $2\times10^{-7}$ rad
for coordinates, $10^{-7}$ rad/s for speeds, $10^{-8}$ for activations, and
$10^{-7}$ m for fiber lengths. A Moco solver status alone is never replay
acceptance; worker states distinguish solve failure, wall or memory stop,
incomplete evidence, replay rejection, and fully audited replay.

At 10 intervals, OpenSim 4.6 `Solve_Succeeded` in 82 iterations with objective
$4.9211583953665505\times10^{-6}$. The independent replay passed the endpoint
check but failed the speed, activation and fiber-length limits: maxima were
$4.278119184863939\times10^{-6}$ rad/s at 0.01 s,
$4.2278841340708667\times10^{-4}$ at 0.001 s, and
$5.394625915713935\times10^{-6}$ m at 0.01 s. Coordinate error was
$1.524035136979407\times10^{-8}$ rad, within its limit. This is an explicitly
failed replay, not a successful model match.

At 20 intervals, the optimizer also returned `Solve_Succeeded` in 122
iterations, objective $4.1654698156426359\times10^{-6}$, and endpoint
$0.3000055857400166$ rad. The integrated replay reached its 30-second
supervisor deadline without writing a replay audit. An earlier separate
no-optimizer replay also reached that deadline, but a wrapper bookkeeping bug
lost its sampled peak RSS. A corrected, separately authorized diagnostic
loaded the exact retained source, request, solution and controls, completed
fresh native replay, and recorded its full timewise state audit. The endpoint
predicate passed with residual $3.80458\times10^{-9}$ rad; the replay failed
speed ($1.01890\times10^{-6}$ rad/s versus $10^{-7}$), activation
($1.15316\times10^{-4}$ versus $10^{-8}$), and fiber length
($1.21692\times10^{-6}$ m versus $10^{-7}$) limits. Coordinate error was
$3.80458\times10^{-9}$ rad, within its $2\times10^{-7}$ limit. The fixed
30-second/1 GiB sampled-peak guard was unchanged; this diagnostic returned
within the wall budget at 210,214,912-byte sampled peak RSS and verified owned
process-tree cleanup.

The replay applied the saved excitation values exactly at every sampled knot.
The request uses Hermite-Simpson transcription with control-mesh interior
interpolation; replay uses piecewise-linear interpolation of saved knots. Those
observations make continuous control representation a testable candidate for
the discrepancy, but do not prove it is causal. The source XML omits the
activation/deactivation constants; their OpenSim 4.6 source defaults are
`0.01/0.04` s, not installed-binary readback. The corrected offline analysis
below narrows this comparison without promoting the failed replay to
qualification.

### Offline Activation Residual Analysis

The source-bound diagnostic in
`docs/development/feedback_controls/experiments/native_moco_mesh20_e1548c5179/activation_residual_analysis.json`
uses the OpenSim 4.6 activation law. For activation $a$, excitation $u$, and
minimum activation $a_{\min}$, it first bounds
$\bar a=\min(1,\max(a,a_{\min}))$, then evaluates
\[
\dot a = \frac{u-\bar a}{\tau},\qquad
\tau = \begin{cases}
\tau_{\mathrm{act}}(0.5+1.5\bar a), & u>\bar a,\\
\tau_{\mathrm{deact}}/(0.5+1.5\bar a), & u\leq\bar a.
\end{cases}
\]
The retained model XML omits `activation_time_constant`,
`deactivation_time_constant`, `minimum_activation`, and
`ignore_activation_dynamics`; the analysis therefore uses 4.6 tag defaults
`0.01 s`, `0.04 s`, `0.01`, and `false`, respectively. The exact source URL is
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/4.6/OpenSim/Actuators/MuscleFirstOrderActivationDynamicModel.cpp`.

The 20-cell mesh has 41 exported rows, arranged as endpoint/midpoint/endpoint
per Hermite-Simpson cell. For each cell width $h$, the reconstruction checks
\[
a_m = \frac{a_k+a_{k+1}}{2} + \frac{h}{8}(f_k-f_{k+1}),\qquad
a_{k+1}-a_k = \frac{h}{6}(f_k+4f_m+f_{k+1}).
\]
The maximum midpoint and Simpson dynamics residuals are `1.1397e-10` and
`2.0774e-9` for flexor, and `1.6274e-11` and `1.7293e-10` for extensor.
Separately, SciPy DOP853 integrates the scalar activation equation across each
saved piecewise-linear input interval. This continuous trace agrees with fresh
native replay within `2.57503e-8` for flexor and `1.98e-15` for extensor.
The optimized flexor activation differs from the replay/scalar trace by up to
`1.15316e-4` at `0.00025 s` and `-8.10477e-5` at the endpoint, despite small
reconstructed collocation residuals. The maximum replay-vs-scalar sensitivity
under tighter tolerances is `3.78e-13`; it is a sensitivity estimate, not a
rigorous integration error bound.

This separates discrete collocation residual from the optimized-state versus
continuous-replay difference, but does not identify its cause. The diagnostic
does not change replay thresholds, invoke a native solver/replay, or qualify
physiology, capture matching, or production execution. It is bound to the
retained source, request, solution, controls and replay audit by the SHA-256
identities in the JSON report.

The 10- and 20-interval optimized coordinate traces differ by at most
$5.66\times10^{-11}$ rad at common time knots, while flexor controls differ by
up to $0.03523$ at those knots. The refinements therefore produce distinct
optimized controls; this comparison does not identify the cause of the
replay-state errors. The exact request, saved arrays, failed replay audit,
timeouts, implementation hashes and reproduction details are retained in
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F07_NATIVE_MOCO_COMPLEXITY_LADDER_TURNOVER.md`.
These bounded synthetic runs establish neither full-body muscle feasibility
nor physiology, capture matching, production replay, OpenSim muscle
qualification, or 17-variant/six-ecosystem parity. All remain unqualified.
